paragraphs: Here's my big idea, friend: God doesn't just notice big gifts, He notices every single one. Twelve leaders came on twelve days, and each one brought the exact same offering. Nobody got a bigger spotlight, and nobody got skipped, because the LORD said, "Each day one leader is to present his offering for the dedication of the altar" (Numbers 7:11). Every tribe got its own turn, and every gift got its own mention (Numbers 7:12-83).

Now look at what happened to the first gift. The LORD told Moses to accept the carts and oxen "that they may be used in the work of the Tent of Meeting" (Numbers 7:5). So what the leaders gave went straight into the work of the Tent, and Moses gave the Gershonites and the Merarites what their service required (Numbers 7:7-8). The Kohathites got none, since they were to carry the holy objects on their shoulders (Numbers 7:9). Same gifts, different jobs, and every gift still went to the work. I once tried to bake with the wrong gear and learned that lesson with a very flat cookie.

The chapter ends with Moses going into the Tent of Meeting to speak with the LORD, and he "heard the voice speaking to him from between the two cherubim above the mercy seat" (Numbers 7:89). The gifts were given, and then the LORD spoke. That's my big idea for you today: give what you have, show up faithfully, and then listen. You don't have to bring more than the next baker, you just have to bring yours.
